one_offs.text: Net gain on equity securities of $9.8B (incl. $8.0B unrealized gain on a private-company stake) added $7.7B to net income and $0.62 to diluted EPS.
Operating margin absorbed a charge for a settlement in principle of certain legal matters (not quantified in the release). Equity-securities gain of $1.3B added $0.95B to net income and $0.08 to EPS.
$3.5B European Commission fine accrued in G&A (Google Services); operating income ex-fine $34,685M (33.9% margin). Equity-securities gain of $10.7B added $8.3B to net income and $0.68 to EPS.
$2.1B Waymo employee-compensation charge (Other Bets, mostly R&D). Equity-securities gain of $2.3B added $1.8B to net income and $0.15 to EPS.
Equity-securities gain of $36.9B (mainly unrealized gains on non-marketable stakes) added $28.7B to net income and $2.35 to EPS.

Equity-securities gain of $99.0B added $77.1B to net income and $6.26 to EPS. Alphabet also raised equity: $20.5B public common offering, $10.0B private placement to a Berkshire Hathaway affiliate and $19.0B of 6.25% mandatory convertible preferred (June 2026).

Equity-securities loss of $8.7B cut net income by $6.7B and EPS by $0.55. 10-Q records a $1.0B charge for EU DMA fines; a $5.2B EU Android fine payment hit cash flow. Preferred dividends reduce net income available to common to $26,170M.

One-time non-cash income-tax charge of $15.93B (valuation allowance on U.S. federal deferred tax assets after the One Big Beautiful Bill Act). Ex-charge: net income $18.64B, diluted EPS $7.25, tax rate 14%.
$8.03B income-tax benefit tied to U.S. Treasury Notice 2026-7 (partial offset to the Q3 2025 charge); EPS ex-benefit $3.13 lower.
$2.40B of legal-proceedings charges and $1.18B of severance tied to the May 2026 reduction (about 8,000 employees). EPS effect not quantified by the company.
$9.89B G&A charge for the August 2026 agreement with 52 state attorneys general on youth-related litigation (payments up to about $18.59B). Ex-charge: operating income $22.88B, diluted EPS $7.40.

commentary.text: Reaffirmed ~$75B 2025 capex plan alongside Q1 results.
Pichai: "we are increasing our investment in capital expenditures in 2025 to approximately $85 billion."
2025 capex range lifted to $91-93B; first $100B revenue quarter. Revenue backlog reached $157.7B (10-Q).
Pichai: 2026 capex "anticipated to be in the range of $175 to $185 billion" - roughly double 2025's $91.4B.
First-party models process more than 16B tokens per minute; "we are compute constrained in the near term"; TPUs to be delivered into select customers' own data centers.
Ashkenazi: 2026 capex range updated to $180-190B; "we expect our 2027 CapEx to significantly increase compared to 2026."
2026 capex raised to $195-205B "to meet demand"; Cloud backlog +$50B QoQ to ~$514B; more third-party capacity in Q3 to pressure Cloud margins modestly.
No buybacks in 1H26; raised ~$49.5B of common and mandatory convertible preferred equity plus multi-currency senior notes to fund AI infrastructure (10-Q Notes 6 and 11).
Gemini app reached 1B users; first-party APIs ~32B tokens/min (+40% QoQ); TPU system sales a "meaningful contributor" to $30.7B Cloud revenue.
2026 capex held at $195-205B; 2027 capex expected to "increase significantly". Backlog $567.7B, just over 55% recognizable within 24 months (10-Q).
Meta AI at almost 1B monthly actives; 2025 capex raised to $64-72B for data centers and servers.
Zuckerberg: "I'm excited to build personal superintelligence for everyone in the world." 2026 expense growth to exceed 2025's rate; another year of significant capex dollar growth.
Meta Superintelligence Labs "off to a great start"; 2026 capex dollar growth "notably larger" than 2025; expense growth significantly faster, led by infrastructure.
FY2026 capex guided to $115-135B (vs $72.2B in 2025) and expenses to $162-169B; 2026 operating income still expected above 2025.
2026 capex raised to $125-145B; release flags youth-related trials that "may ultimately result in a material loss."
May 2026 headcount reduction (~8,000 roles, $1.18B severance); buybacks paused since Q4 2025; long-term debt rose to $83.66B.
Muse personal agents set up by 10M+ people in US/Canada; Muse cost efficiency to improve "more than 10x in the next year"; GEM ranking lifted app-ad conversions 9.6%.

2026 capex narrowed to $135-145B; no 2027 capex or expense outlook yet ("still developing our budget and capacity plans"); infrastructure costs up on third-party cloud, depreciation and data-center opex.

risks.title: U.S. Search remedies on appeal
risks.text: Final judgment entered Dec 2025; Google appealed (Jan 2026) and DOJ/states cross-appealed (Feb 2026).

risks.title: U.S. ad tech remedies
risks.text: Sep 2026: court denied DOJ's structural divestiture request and ordered behavioral remedies; Google plans to appeal the liability ruling.

risks.title: EU fines and DMA
risks.text: Android fine (EUR 4.1B) paid ($5.2B) Jul 2026; EUR 3.0B ad tech fine under appeal; Jul 2026 DMA fines of EUR 430M (Play) and EUR 460M (Search), $1.0B charge in Q3 2026.

risks.title: AI Mode monetization
risks.text: Management cited lower monetization of AI Mode queries and FX as Search growth slowed to 12% in Q3 2026 from 17% in Q2.

risks.title: Negative free cash flow and dilution
risks.text: FCF of -$5.9B (Q2 2026) and -$9.1B (Q3 2026); buybacks halted since Q1 2026 while common, preferred and ATM equity was issued.

risks.title: Cloud backlog conversion and TPU sales
risks.text: Backlog of $567.7B (up from $92.4B at Q1 2025); TPU system sales expected to ramp more meaningfully in 2027.

risks.title: Youth-safety litigation
risks.text: Aug 2026 agreement with 52 state AGs (payments up to ~$18.59B, $9.89B charged in Q3); further U.S. youth trials scheduled in coming months.

risks.title: EU DMA ad model
risks.text: EC found the subscription-for-no-ads model non-compliant (Apr 2025); Meta warned changes could significantly affect European revenue.

risks.title: FTC monopolization case
risks.text: District court ruled for Meta (Nov 2025); FTC said in Jan 2026 it would appeal.

risks.title: Expense and capex step-up
risks.text: FY2026 expenses guided to $175-179B (vs $117.7B in 2025) and capex to $135-145B; Q3 2026 FCF was -$2.1B.

risks.title: User growth deceleration
risks.text: DAP growth slowed to 3% YoY (3.64B); Q1 2026 dip attributed to internet disruptions in Iran and Russia's WhatsApp restriction.

risks.title: Muse agents and Reality Labs path
risks.text: Muse rolling to glasses; Reality Labs losses guided to $18-19B in 2026 and about $15B in 2027. Two-for-one-effect Class C stock dividend after Jan 19, 2027 charter amendment.

a_geo_note.2025Q4: Derived: FY2025 (10-K) minus nine months 2025 (Q3 2025 10-Q); sums to $113,829M vs $113,828M in the release ($1M rounding).

apac_commentary.text: Susan Li: "Asia-based e-commerce exporters" cut spend on Meta ahead of the end of the U.S. de minimis exemption; overall spend for those advertisers was "below the levels prior to April." Asia-Pacific ad revenue (user geography) grew 12%, the slowest region.
APAC revenue grew 12% reported and 15% in constant currency; 10-Q: "APAC revenue growth was unfavorably affected by changes in foreign currency exchange rates."
APAC revenue grew 19% reported and 18% in constant currency; APAC share of revenue rose to 17% from 16%.
Asia-Pacific impressions +23% with price per ad +1%: the region added volume at low prices while US & Canada (+13%) and Europe (+19%) drove price.
Asia-Pacific price per ad fell 2% YoY, the only regional decline in the period, while impressions grew 24%.

Susan Li: price growth "partially offset by strong impression growth, particularly from lower-monetizing surfaces and regions." Asia-Pacific: impressions +14%, price per ad +1%, ad revenue +15% vs +26% worldwide.
APAC revenue (customer billing address) grew 11.7% to $19.9B while the United States grew 38.8%; APAC fell to 15.6% of revenue from 17.4% a year earlier.

apac_risks.title: Japan: JFTC cease-and-desist order
apac_risks.text: Apr 15, 2025 order under the Antimonopoly Act ends MADA/RSA conditions that required Google Search and Chrome preinstallation on Android; independent monitor for five years.

apac_risks.title: Japan: Mobile Software Competition Act
apac_risks.text: Google designated for OS, app store, browser and search engine (Mar 2025); full enforcement from Dec 18, 2025, with prohibited conduct and obligations for designated providers.

apac_risks.title: Australia: under-16 social media minimum age
apac_risks.text: From Dec 10, 2025, age-restricted platforms include Facebook, Instagram, Threads and YouTube; corporate penalties up to 150,000 penalty units (about A$49.5M).

apac_risks.title: India: WhatsApp data-sharing case
apac_risks.text: Nov 2025: NCLAT set aside CCI's five-year ban on WhatsApp sharing user data with Meta for advertising but upheld the Rs 213.14 crore penalty.

apac_risks.title: APAC price per ad near flat
apac_risks.text: Asia-Pacific price per ad has grown 5% or less in every quarter since Q1 2025 (Q4 2025: -2%), versus +23% in US & Canada in Q3 2026; APAC growth depends on impression volume.

apac_risks.title: APAC-based exporters as advertisers
apac_risks.text: On a customer-address basis Asia-Pacific was $53.8B (27%) of Meta's 2025 revenue versus $39.3B (20%) by user location: about $14.6B came from APAC-billed advertisers reaching users elsewhere, exposed to trade policy (de minimis, tariffs).

apac_risks.title: APAC slowing inside Alphabet's mix
apac_risks.text: APAC growth slowed to 11.7% in Q3 2026 from 23.1% in Q1 2026 while U.S. revenue (including TPU-driven Cloud) accelerated; APAC's 15.6% share of revenue is the lowest since at least Q1 2024.
